branch_scope: separate from PR189 frozen Ecology submission and PR195 stationary-source audit
question: After a change in physically usable Antarctic breeding habitat, does attraction/settlement respond differently from offspring survival and subsequent recruitment, and can that mismatch be caused by event timing rather than static island area?

stage_specific_independent_endpoint_requ.pre_choice_habitat: date-specific physical platform/accessibility mapped independently of observed birds or nests, before settlement
stage_specific_independent_endpoint_requ.settlement: detection-corrected breeder attempts or identified founders with known origin, not guano or named colony label
stage_specific_independent_endpoint_requ.reproductive_fitness: nest/egg/chick outcome aligned to the same physical patch and reproductive stage
stage_specific_independent_endpoint_requ.recruitment_debt: known birth cohort later recorded as first breeder with natal origin, detection and dispersal modeled
stage_specific_independent_endpoint_requ.comparison: at least two independent timed disturbances with credible within-system unexposed controls
stage_specific_independent_endpoint_requ.identity: same site/colony/nest identifier across exposure, settlement, outcome and recruitment datasets

novelty_prior_art.claim: Adult or nesting-like aggregation can occur on ephemeral fast ice; disturbance can destroy it
novelty_prior_art.source: LaRue et al 2019 doi:10.1017/S095410201900018X (2018 Cape Crozier apparent fast-ice subcolony: 426 birds; eggs unverified)

novelty_prior_art.claim: iceberg physically blocks emperor penguin colony access and suppresses chick numbers
novelty_prior_art.source: Park et al 2026 doi:10.1038/s43247-026-03764-w (Coulman 2025 ~69% chick-count decline)

novelty_prior_art.claim: nest structure correlates with survival, especially when moisture/snow is high
novelty_prior_art.source: McLatchie et al 2024 doi:10.1002/ece3.10988; 450 Adelie nests/10 years across Windmill Islands

novelty_prior_art.claim: human station removal allows Adelie penguins to reoccupy breeding land
novelty_prior_art.source: Kim et al 2023 doi:10.3390/d15010051 (Cape Hallett 1960/1983/2019 nests)

novelty_prior_art.claim: habitat change redistributes nests within a colony after exceptional waves
novelty_prior_art.source: Kim et al 2026 doi:10.1002/jgo2.70001 (Edmonson mainland, 2019 event)

forbidden_shortcuts: Do not interpret approximate colony coordinate as dated breeding footprint
Do not join whole-island chick totals onto specific nest GPS locations
Do not treat reproductive behavior or chicks present as a confirmed new colony or first recruitment
Do not infer hatch/fledge success from attendance guano or ice classes
Do not relabel known ice access/snow/nest structure correlations as 2026 novel causal effects
Do not use missing surveys as zero
Do not reinterpret exploratory PR195 outputs as prospectively pre-registered outcomes
Do not change locked PR189 frozen Ecology submission
minimum_new_data_before_fitting: At least one external, independently dated crosswalk with pre-choice physical exposure, same-patch settlement and chick production; multiple independent perturbations and stage-aware controls required for a general island rule; known-age recruits additionally required for recruitment debt
